On Wed, Aug 19, 2026 at 08:12 AM ops@orionhealth.com wrote:
> We're seeing a broad increase in 504 and 429 responses from the Redwood hosted endpoints...

Quick triage notes:
- Error profile: high 429s then rising 504s and connection timeouts.
- Host-level metrics: GPU utilization is normal; request queue depth on several frontends is high (>95th percentile).
- Trace sampling shows long wait time in request_queue before runtime scheduling; once scheduled, processing looks normal for successful requests.

Hypothesis: aggressive prefix/KV cache eviction + continuous batching changes in yesterday's runtime library might be causing cache thrash. That would increase downstream cache misses, increase per-request work variance, and lead to queue saturation and client retries amplifying the problem.

Next steps I'm running:
1) Roll back the batching/kv-cache heuristics we rolled out in canary at 03:00 PDT (will flip the feature flag if rollback is judged safe).
2) Temporarily raise our per-route concurrency and apply short-term rate-limiting for Orion to stabilize.

I will apply the FF and post results.

— Monica
Sr. Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: markus_klein@redwood.ai
To: monica_patel@redwood.ai, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai, ops@orionhealth.com
Date: 2026-08-19T09:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Production spike — many 504s and 429s across inference endpoints

Folks — running summary of the bug: the new prefix-aware KV eviction logic added a race where concurrent writes for hot prefixes temporarily evict fresh entries; this in turn forces the runtime to rebuild KV cache more often, raising tail latency for those requests. With our batching window tightened, we now see bursts where request processing time multiplies and queueing pushes requests past proxy timeouts (resulting in 504s).

Mitigation steps taken at 08:45:
- Flipped feature flag: disabled the new eviction heuristic across the affected clusters (canary->prod).
- Increased per-route worker pool for Orion routes by +30% to drain queues.
- Applied short-term circuit-breaker to reject retries beyond a shallow backoff to break amplification loops.

Preliminary metrics (08:50 -> 09:00): error rate dropped from 18% 5xx to ~3% 5xx; tail latency (p99) reduced from ~4.8s to 380ms.

I'm pushing a hotfix to make eviction conservative and will schedule a postmortem. Will coordinate a rollback window and a controlled re-release once we have a robust cache-coherence guard.

— Markus Klein
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime
